name: Modern liberalism in the United States
summary: American modern liberalism favors a mixed economy in which government regulates markets, manages the economy, and provides social insurance, healthcare and education. It couples this with civil rights, civil liberties, secular government and social equality for women, minorities and LGBT people. It rests on the view that freedom requires economic security as well as freedom from interference.
scope: The mainstream tradition from the Progressive Era and Franklin Roosevelt's New Deal through the Great Society to the contemporary Democratic Party program, with theoretical grounding in new liberalism (T. H. Green, Dewey) and Rawls. It excludes classical liberalism and what Americans call libertarianism, and the democratic socialist left.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Liberals back a government role in guaranteeing care, from FDR's right to medical care to expanding the ACA, though mainstream platforms stop short of a single state system.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The party program commits to a federal minimum of at least $15 an hour, and minimum wage laws are a standard liberal policy.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Liberals prefer a mixed economy in which government corrects market failures and manages the macroeconomy.

public-ownership.rationale: Modern liberals favor regulation and social insurance within a mixed economy rather than nationalizing industries.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The platform proposes a minimum tax on billionaires, higher corporate rates and ending the capital gains preference for millionaires.

unions-good.rationale: The platform backs the PRO Act, public-sector bargaining and penalties for union busting.

property-fundamental.rationale: New liberals hold that property rights can entrench unequal power and so may be limited for social ends.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Liberals want government to keep competition alive and curb monopolies, as in the platform's antitrust record.

cut-welfare.rationale: Liberals seek to expand the safety net, not cut it.

worker-ownership.rationale: Worker ownership is not part of the mainstream program, which relies on regulation and bargaining.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Liberals stress civil liberties; the program only addresses privacy narrowly, so this is inferred.

legalize-drugs.rationale: The party backs rescheduling and expunging marijuana convictions but has no program for legalizing recreational drugs generally.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The program combats hate crimes and hate groups but liberals broadly defend First Amendment protection of speech; inferred.

strong-leader.rationale: Liberals emphasize democracy, rule of law and constitutional limits.

state-harmful.rationale: Liberals see government as a necessary instrument for liberty and welfare.

limit-guns.rationale: The platform pledges an assault weapons ban, universal background checks, safe storage and red flag laws.

empower-police-military.rationale: The platform funds more officers and a strong military while also restricting police practices and pushing reform.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; liberal opinion is split.

decide-locally.rationale: Liberals typically rely on national action for civil rights, social insurance and regulation.

rehabilitation.rationale: The platform would end private prisons and restrict solitary confinement, reflecting a reform orientation.

traditional-family.rationale: Liberals support LGBT equality and diverse family forms rather than a privileged traditional model.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The platform celebrates the Respect for Marriage Act and pledges the Equality Act.

abortion-legal.rationale: The platform pledges to restore the right to choose; reproductive rights are a core liberal position.

more-religion-public.rationale: Liberals support free exercise alongside strict separation of church and state.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Liberals back civil rights, affirmative action and closing the racial wealth gap.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The program protects gender-affirming care and LGBTQ equality, implying a view of gender as not purely biological; inferred.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Liberals emphasize pluralism and civil rights over cultural preservation; inferred.

gradual-change.rationale: Liberal reform runs through democratic institutions, from the New Deal to the ACA, but its adherents do not prize gradualism as such.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The platform seeks more legal visas, refugee resettlement and a path to citizenship while also strengthening border enforcement.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The program stresses alliances and multilateral institutions but does not call for more power for the UN.

free-trade.rationale: The platform backs targeted tariffs and trade deals with labor and climate standards while opposing broad tariffs.

nation-first.rationale: The program stresses alliances such as NATO and multilateral cooperation.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: The program promotes human rights abroad but calls force a last resort.

open-borders.rationale: The platform calls for securing the border and enforcement capacity.

limit-growth.rationale: Liberals treat environmental investment as compatible with long-run prosperity and growth.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: The platform sets net-zero by 2050 and large clean-energy investment through the Inflation Reduction Act.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Liberals invest in technology but do not hold that it will solve most problems; inferred.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; liberal opinion is mixed.

revolution-justified.rationale: Liberals pursue change through democratic and constitutional means.

experts-over-public.rationale: Progressive-era liberalism valued expertise, yet liberals also stress democracy; adherents differ.

central-planning.rationale: Liberals favor a mixed economy with market competition.

socialized-markets.rationale: Liberals do not make worker or public ownership a condition of acceptable markets.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not part of the liberal program, which favors progressive income taxes.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Progressive taxation to reduce inequality implies support for taxing wealth transfers; inferred.

basic-income.rationale: Mainstream liberal programs favor targeted benefits, child care and social insurance over an unconditional income.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The platform backs targeted tariffs on Chinese goods and Buy America rules but opposes broad tariffs.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The platform backs public investment in clean energy and strategic industries.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Rawls's property-owning democracy points this way but is not mainstream liberal policy.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Liberals favor a mixed economy with wages and money.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Liberal macroeconomics uses Keynesian management of the economy.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Liberals favor free collective bargaining, not state-recognized bodies setting prices.

one-party-rule.rationale: Liberals stress democracy and civil liberties.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Liberalism grounds authority in democratic consent.

democracy-best.rationale: Democracy and the rule of law are core liberal commitments.

direct-votes.rationale: Liberals mainly work through representative institutions; inferred.

workers-councils.rationale: Liberals reject replacing parliaments with councils.

right-to-secede.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from commitment to national institutions.

natural-rulers.rationale: Liberals hold that all are equal before the law.

political-violence-never.rationale: Liberals reject political violence but accept force in defense or war, so this is inferred.

war-builds-character.rationale: The program treats force as a last resort.

separate-church-state.rationale: The platform pledges to protect free exercise while maintaining separation of church and state.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Liberals hold to church-state separation and public reason.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Modern liberals favour an active state that provides public goods, which implies keeping courts, policing and defence public; privatising them is not seriously debated in the sources.

military-superiority.rationale: The program backs a strong military and alliances; superiority is inferred.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Liberals support civil rights, immigration and equal status regardless of ethnicity.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Liberals reject class conflict as the basic driver of history.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Liberals seek to reduce inequality but frame the aim as opportunity and a floor, with Rawls allowing inequalities that help the worst off.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not covered in the sources; inferred from liberal support for minority rights.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents differ.

civilizational-union.rationale: Liberals reject political union by religion or civilization.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Liberals prioritize individual rights and civil liberties.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Liberals support protecting the environment; the grounds are mostly instrumental, so inferred.

limit-population.rationale: Not part of liberal policy; inferred from liberal emphasis on reproductive rights.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Modern liberalism seeks to spread the gains of industrial prosperity through regulation and welfare rather than reject industry; the sources do not take up the primitivist claim.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Not a liberal tenet; inferred from institutional reformism.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Inferred from emphasis on democratic accountability and rule of law.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Inferred from liberal emphasis on privacy and civil liberties.

restore-past-order.rationale: Liberalism is a reform tradition oriented to progress.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Dewey-style pragmatism and policy experimentation are strands in the tradition, though not universal.

direct-action.rationale: Liberals pursue change through elections and legislation.

means-match-ends.rationale: Liberal reliance on democratic means follows from its ends; inferred.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Liberals accept specialization and modern industrial organization.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Liberals support a social minimum but not distribution by need as a general rule.

production-for-use.rationale: Liberals accept profit-driven markets under regulation.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Liberals accept profit as legitimate while regulating abuses.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Modern liberals defend constitutional democracy and individual rights, which rules out class dictatorship, though the sources do not discuss the Marxist idea.

collective-farming.rationale: Not a liberal policy; FDR's program supports farmers' decent returns.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Modern liberals regulate capitalism rather than see it as a cause of war, and back open trade and alliances; the Leninist thesis is not discussed in the sources.

taxation-theft.rationale: Liberals fund social programs through progressive taxation.

harm-principle.rationale: Liberals broadly accept limits on liberty grounded in harm, while also accepting some paternalism such as safety regulation.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Liberals support group-targeted civil rights remedies, though individual rights are foundational.

conscription.rationale: Not in the program; inferred from civil liberties emphasis.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Liberals prize democratic participation and voting rights.

state-as-business.rationale: Liberals see citizens as members, not customers, with social rights.

positive-liberty.rationale: FDR and new liberal theory hold that freedom requires economic security and material means.

media-academia-power.rationale: Liberals do not hold this view; inferred.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Liberals reject racial hierarchy and support civil rights.

total-state.rationale: Liberals stress civil liberties and limits on the state.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Liberals reject territorial aggrandizement; the program backs sovereignty.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The Stanford Encyclopedia's account of liberalism holds that political authority must be justified to the free and equal people subject to it, rooted in consent and the rule of law rather than personal bonds.

bound-labor.rationale: Liberals reject bound labor and support worker rights.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Liberals generally accept shared standards of reason; inferred.

universal-morality.rationale: Rawls holds that basic human rights apply to all peoples, though he grounds liberalism in public reason; inferred.

single-common-good.rationale: Liberal politics is usually seen as balancing plural interests and conceptions of the good.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The platform supports Israel's security and a two-state solution.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from liberal emphasis on equal citizenship and immigration rules.

workplace-democracy.rationale: The program backs unions and bargaining rather than votes on company governance.

school-vouchers.rationale: The platform opposes private-school vouchers and similar programs.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Keynesian macroeconomic management endorses stimulus when needed.

economic-freedom.rationale: New liberals hold that political freedom rests on security and that market freedom alone does not secure liberty.

rule-by-example.rationale: Liberals rely on law and democratic institutions.

national-self-determination.rationale: Inferred from Wilsonian roots and support for sovereignty such as Ukraine's.

force-without-un.rationale: Adherents are split; the platform calls force a last resort without addressing UN authorization.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Liberals protect religious freedom and do not call for reason alone; inferred.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: The platform supports expanded legal immigration and citizenship, but benefit eligibility is not addressed.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Liberals favor expanding safety-net programs without added work requirements.

class-collaboration.rationale: Liberals favor bargaining and regulation within capitalism over class struggle.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The 2024 platform calls the arts and humanities part of America's DNA and touts federal help that kept libraries, theaters and concert halls afloat, so it backs inherited cultural institutions.

dominated-front.rationale: Liberals favor alliances with Western powers.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Liberals support women's rights and equal legal treatment.

ban-interest.rationale: Modern liberals regulate lending to protect consumers but accept credit markets; a ban on interest is not discussed in the sources.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Liberals support civil rights and voting rights.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Liberals see the state as a democratic instrument of the public.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: The platform would eliminate oil and gas subsidies and pushes clean energy.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The program stresses pluralism and rights for immigrants; inferred.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy theory liberals reject; the platform condemns white nationalist ideas.

national-mission.rationale: The program supports democracy promotion but not a national mission to spread its form of government.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Liberals support women's rights and equal pay agendas premised on structural disadvantage.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Liberals defend democratic institutions while backing anti-corruption measures.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Contradicts liberal rights to reproductive choice and equality.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The platform backs policing reform and accountability measures.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Liberals support a social minimum and regulation.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Contradicts liberal equal rights and civil rights.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Equal rights and civil rights are central to the platform and tradition.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Not a liberal question; liberals reject the premise.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Inferred from rule of law and equal protection.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The 2024 platform pledges to protect the First Amendment right to free exercise of religion for everyone and to keep church and state separate, which excludes legal limits on conversion.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A secular state in the liberal view does not write one faith's dietary rules into law; the question has no place in the sources or US debate.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Church-state separation implies no state religious instruction.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Liberals do not hold this doctrine.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Liberal theory grounds legitimate authority in consent and democracy.

trade-surplus.rationale: Liberals do not embrace mercantilist export targets.

population-transfer.rationale: Pressuring a minority to leave conflicts with the equal rights and civil-rights commitments of modern liberalism; expulsions are not discussed.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Liberals accept state coercion for taxes and regulation.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Liberals credit cooperation, institutions and public investment as well as competition; this is inferred.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Civil liberties emphasis suggests wariness of banning parties; inferred.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Close to the new liberal view that unequal power undermines freedom, though not the republican formula.

separated-powers.rationale: Rule of law and constitutional checks are core liberal commitments.

vanguard-party.rationale: Modern liberals work through democratic elections and reform, which is incompatible with vanguard rule; Leninist party theory is not discussed in the sources.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Rawls's difference principle and the safety-net agenda favor the least advantaged.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Liberals favor public housing support; sale of public housing is not a program aim.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: The platform backs the PRO Act and opposes union-weakening laws.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Liberals attribute poverty to institutions and economic policy.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The platform's racial-equity and anti-hate commitments and its support for legal immigration imply rejecting this claim, though it does not address diversity and cohesion directly.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Liberals rely on elections and appointment by merit; lotteries for office are not part of the platform or tradition.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Civil liberties and due process are core liberal commitments, and the party program opposes suspending rights even in a crisis.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Liberals back government intervention such as anti-gouging rules, but mainstream platforms do not call for fixed food prices; adherents are split, inferred.

party-controls-media.rationale: Press freedom and independent media are central liberal commitments, and the program backs a free and independent press.

party-commands-army.rationale: Liberal constitutionalism holds that the military serves the state under civilian, constitutional control, independent of any party.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: The party program favors a pathway to citizenship and a more welcoming immigration system, not long waits.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Mainstream liberalism accepts competitive official salaries and has no doctrine tying pay to a worker wage; inferred from its mixed-economy, institutional approach.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: The Democratic Party is a loose coalition whose legislators vote on their own judgment and constituents; binding discipline is not a liberal principle (inferred).

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The platform favors alliances and multilateral cooperation, but US liberals rarely endorse binding supranational bodies; inferred.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Liberal constitutionalism rests on checks and balances, and the platform stresses congressional and legal limits on presidential power.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Liberalism holds church governance to be a private matter for believers, with no view favoring hierarchy; inferred from its separation of church and state.

clerical-rule.rationale: The platform and the liberal tradition insist on secular government and separation of church and state.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Mainstream liberals back national defense and alliances and do not endorse revolutionary defeatism.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Civil liberties, including free expression, are core to modern liberalism, which rejects state censorship of art on moral grounds.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: American liberals generally accept the two-term limit as a safeguard against entrenchment; the platform does not address it, so this is inferred.

recall-officials.rationale: Progressive Era liberals introduced recall in several states, but the national platform does not address it; inferred as moderate support.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The party platform backs NATO and alliance commitments, so liberals generally reject withdrawal.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Liberals support rental housing and tenant protections and subsidies for renters, with ownership as one option among several.

people-in-arms.rationale: The platform supports gun safety laws and a professional military, so an armed citizenry in place of the army is rejected.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Liberal thought does not hold that rural life is morally healthier; inferred from its urban, pluralist base.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Not addressed by liberalism as a program; adherents have no common position on border-drawn reunification.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Liberals value education and expertise and tend to reject the claim that the educated are out of touch.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Liberal multiculturalism and cultural relativism respect all cultures as equal, though some liberals still rank civilizations on rights.

death-penalty.rationale: The Democratic Party platform now calls for abolishing the federal death penalty, and the majority of liberals oppose it.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: The party program backs comprehensive sex education and gender equality in schools.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Secular government and the separation of church and state lead liberals to oppose teaching creationism in public schools.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Liberals prioritise civil liberties and free expression, though some back limits on obscenity; most oppose restricting porn by law.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Liberals back birthright citizenship and defend the Fourteenth Amendment's citizenship by birth on the territory.

minority-language-support.rationale: Liberals support language access in public services and bilingual education, as part of minority rights and inclusion.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Liberals are split between religious liberty and equality concerns, such as exemptions from anti-discrimination law.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: The liberal tradition from Mill values individuality and tolerance of diverse ways of living.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Liberals back debt relief for the poorest in some programs, but there is no settled doctrine of outright cancellation; adherents are split.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred from the liberal view of reform within a market economy; liberals favor economic aid and fair rules but not transforming the property system.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Liberals defend the existing Constitution and amend it by regular procedure, yet some back reforms such as a convention; no common line is stated, inferred.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Civil rights and civil liberties are core liberal commitments, and the platform defends democratic freedoms, so trading them for growth is rejected.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: The platform supports global health, development and humanitarian aid, though mainstream liberals do not make it a strict duty equal to that at home.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: The party platform keeps the US deterrent and alliances, and an independent deterrent is not a live liberal issue; inferred.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Many liberals favor abolishing the Electoral College for a national popular vote, but this is not a settled party plank; inferred from democratic-equality principles.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Liberals broadly accept an independent Federal Reserve while some on the left want it to serve employment goals; adherents are split.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Mainstream liberals back a two-state solution involving territorial compromise, so they lean against holding land at the cost of peace; inferred.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: New liberalism and the New Deal accept regulation, taxation and limits on property in the public interest, though private property itself is kept.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Mainstream liberals mostly saw the USSR as a communist dictatorship rather than as state capitalism and would not adopt the label; inferred.

precautionary-principle.rationale: The party program commits to strong environmental regulation and climate action that does not wait for full certainty.

collective-defense.rationale: The platform treats US commitments to NATO and allies as ironclad, including mutual defense.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Inferred from liberal support for self-determination and for opposing Russia's annexations; the tradition has no doctrine on the point.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Liberals defend secular government and the separation of church and state, and religious freedom rather than state control of churches.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Inferred: the American president is a partisan leader and liberals accept that, rather than seeking a ceremonial unifier.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Not addressed by the tradition; inferred as split between the Unionist heritage and liberal respect for self-determination.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Inferred from the liberal support for federalism and state-level policy variation within the union.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Secular government is a core liberal commitment and a sacred ruler is wholly foreign to it.

flat-income-tax.rationale: The platform calls for the wealthy and corporations to pay more, and liberals back progressive income taxation.

character-from-environment.rationale: New liberalism and Dewey stress that education and social conditions shape people, which grounds liberal social policy.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Rule of law and equal subjection of officeholders to the law are central to liberalism.

space-expansion.rationale: Inferred: the platform supports NASA but liberals generally put Earth's problems first and do not make space a central goal.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Inferred from the Madisonian tradition of checks and balances that liberals inherit; the idea is not a stated liberal aim.

leader-cult.rationale: Liberalism treats leaders as ordinary officeholders and rejects leader worship.

equal-parenting.rationale: Adherents are split between shared-parenting reform and concern for case-by-case child-centred decisions; the platform is silent.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist thesis; inferred from liberalism's mixed economy and rejection of revolutionary socialism.

land-redistribution.rationale: Inferred from liberalism's acceptance of private property under regulation and rejection of expropriation.

refugee-return.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the platform's humanitarian and refugee-protection stance.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Inferred from the platform's support for territorial integrity and the international order.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Religious freedom and church-state separation are core to the platform and liberal thought.

women-must-cover.rationale: Secular government and women's equality oppose compelled dress.

common-currency.rationale: Not a US question; adherents have no settled view on monetary unions.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Inferred from a civic rather than ancestral conception of nationhood.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Inferred from support for pluralism and minority cultural rights, though within a common state.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Inferred from the civil-rights tradition of seeking equality where one lives.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The tradition stresses policy and moral reform, not strict economic determinism; inferred from its theory.

ban-cartels.rationale: The platform backs antitrust enforcement and curbing corporate concentration.

no-bailouts.rationale: Modern liberals have accepted rescues, such as in the 2008 crisis, while criticising bailouts without conditions.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Liberalism holds that courts protect rights against majorities, as in civil-rights decisions.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: The platform supports women's representation, but mandated quotas on public bodies are not a settled position.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The tradition supports trade and open markets and rejects autarky.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: The 2024 platform ties trade to worker and environmental protection, though I did not confirm the exact wording.

moral-incentives.rationale: Inferred from the New Deal reliance on wages and material security, not moral appeals.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Inferred from commitment to constitutional democracy and rejection of political violence.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Inferred from commitment to equality; the US Constitution already bans titles of nobility.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Liberals favor inclusive, multi-perspective history teaching over a nation-centred narrative; inferred from platform emphasis on diversity.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Modern liberalism rests on equality and self-determination, and its platform rejects imperial-style rule of other peoples.

patriotic-education.rationale: Liberals are split between civic pride and concern over nationalist teaching; no party line.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: The Democratic platform supports affirmative action and race-conscious efforts to widen opportunity.

public-money-creation.rationale: Liberals accept the existing central bank and banking system, though some progressives float public banking; inferred.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The New Deal tradition holds that regulation and social insurance let capitalism survive its crises.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Liberal foreign policy stresses partnership, not special claims over former imperial spheres; inferred.

delink-world-market.rationale: Liberals favor trade, aid and integration with managed rules, not delinking; inferred.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Liberalism does not treat workers as a class divided by imperial exploitation; inferred.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The platform backs civil rights and anti-discrimination law covering public accommodation, hiring and housing.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Liberals prize constitutionally protected civil rights and liberties, and Rawlsian liberalism gives rights priority over majorities.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Inferred from liberal support for self-determination and Indigenous rights in the party program; treaty voidness is not itself stated.

elective-rulers.rationale: Liberalism descends from the social-contract tradition in which government rests on the consent of the governed, and American liberals defend republican elections.

minority-veto.rationale: Liberalism pairs majority rule with protected individual rights; it does not give any single member a veto over collective decisions.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The liberal tradition from Locke holds that rulers who violate the law and the public trust may legitimately be resisted or replaced.

parliament-supreme.rationale: American liberals reject monarchy and support legislative lawmaking under the constitution, though with courts and a separate executive; inferred.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Not a central plank; inferred from the party program's general support for animal welfare protections and humane treatment.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred: mainstream liberals accept animal use for food and research with welfare regulation rather than abolition.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Liberals argue the wealthy should pay a fair share through taxes to support others; the duty is framed as civic and legal rather than aristocratic. Inferred.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The program stresses voting rights, civic participation and an active citizenry, the opposite of withdrawal.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Liberals generally see media as a pluralist public sphere; the pacification thesis belongs to critical theory. Inferred.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: The consent-through-culture thesis is a Marxist (Gramscian) claim; mainstream liberals describe power as pluralist and electorally accountable. Inferred.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Liberals favor open trade, aid and investment as routes to development, not dependency theory. Inferred from the party program.

native-born-offices.rationale: Liberals support equal citizenship and oppose reserving offices by birth, beyond the constitution's presidential requirement.

party-own-road.rationale: The ideology is indifferent to communist party strategy; no position is stated.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: The party program supports foreign assistance and investment in developing countries.

return-lost-territory.rationale: The program upholds territorial integrity and the rules-based international order rather than irredentist claims.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Liberals support tribal sovereignty and equal rights but not political rule by one descent group over others. Inferred.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Liberals regard opposition to fascism as consistent with democratic values; not stated as a constitutional doctrine. Inferred.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Cold War liberalism, a main strand, condemned both fascism and communism as totalitarian; inferred.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Inferred from mainstream historiography and the liberal commitment to racial equality, which attribute the war to slavery.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Liberals increasingly favor removing or recontextualizing monuments to figures such as Confederate leaders; inferred from program stance on racial justice.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Liberals are split: concern for boys and men sits beside a program focused on women's and minorities' disadvantage.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: The program emphasizes protection for women victims (VAWA); equal-service symmetry is not a liberal position. Inferred.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Liberals hold that human rights and constitutional democracy are universal, not civilization-specific.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Liberalism requires civilian control of the military and a nonpolitical armed forces.

paid-care-work.rationale: The program backs paid family leave and higher pay and recognition for care workers.

filial-duty.rationale: Liberals value family but stress individual autonomy and public social insurance over legal duties; adherents are split.

office-by-exam.rationale: Merit civil service is accepted, but democratic elections and diverse hiring are also valued; split.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Mainstream Democrats support national-security screening of foreign investment in strategic sectors; inferred.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Individual autonomy in personal life is a core liberal principle and no-fault divorce is established law.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Representative government with independent judgment is the norm; recall is a Progressive Era device used rarely; inferred.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Liberals defended Social Security against privatisation into individual accounts.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Private property in a mixed economy is accepted; community or use-based land tenure is outside the program; inferred.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Legislative control of the budget is a basic constitutional principle liberals uphold; inferred.

single-official-language.rationale: Liberals oppose English-only measures and support language access for minorities; inferred.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Liberals generally oppose blanket restrictions on foreigners; inferred.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Civil-rights enforcement tradition treats unjustified disparate outcomes as discrimination; contested among adherents.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Liberals are split between concern over inequality and waste and acceptance of consumer culture.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Liberals generally favour diplomacy and multilateral limits on covert war; inferred.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Liberals oppose unilateral intervention against an ally's sovereignty; inferred.

corporate-influence.rationale: The Democratic platform calls for curbing the power of big money in politics, including overturning Citizens United and more disclosure.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Liberals support transparency about foreign money in politics but also defend academic and press openness; no settled view on restricting NGO or media funding.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Liberals back child tax credits and family support but frame them around child poverty, and favor immigration over population-decline concerns; split.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred from the liberal commitment to housing access, mobility and anti-exclusion; restricting buyers by residence cuts against these.

job-guarantee.rationale: FDR's Second Bill of Rights named a right to a useful job, but the party platform emphasizes job creation rather than a federal employer of last resort; adherents are split.

democratic-peace.rationale: Liberal internationalism holds that democracies seldom fight each other and the platform backs democratic partners and institutions, though with less emphasis on spreading democracy by force.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Mainstream liberals, following Rawls, hold a natural duty to support just institutions, while accepting civil disobedience as a limited exception.

non-intervention.rationale: The platform defends alliances, sanctions and support for Ukraine, and liberals accept humanitarian intervention in some cases.

industrial-unions.rationale: The platform strongly supports unions but takes no position on industrial versus craft organization.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Liberalism's civil rights commitment rejects the claim that an ethnic or religious minority is conspiring against the nation.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The platform defends marriage equality, which presupposes marriage as a legal institution carrying benefits and rights.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Open government and freedom of information are long-standing liberal commitments, and the platform supports transparency.

local-production.rationale: Liberals back local food and farmers' markets but also trade and global supply chains; not a doctrine, so split.

informal-organisation.rationale: American liberals work through parties, unions and advocacy groups, and the platform treats these as the vehicles of political change.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Liberals generally support international law and institutions, though accepting US constitutional supremacy in practice; inferred and mixed.

religious-nation.rationale: Modern liberalism stresses secular government and equal standing for all faiths and none, so a religiously defined nation is rejected.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Inferred: American liberalism treats states as sovereign equals bound by law, not by ritual tribute, even while backing alliances.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Liberal programs rely on federal pooling and transfers across states and regions according to need; inferred from the platform.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Modern liberalism keeps a mixed economy with private property and rejects common ownership of the means of production.

defeat-communism.rationale: Cold War liberalism favoured containment, but the current program deals with communist states through diplomacy and competition; inferred.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Liberal healthcare and education policy funds services through mixed public and private providers, as in the Affordable Care Act.

religion-illusion.rationale: Liberalism is secular but protects religious freedom and does not hold that religion is an illusion; inferred.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Liberals defend a regulated market economy and credit it with prosperity while seeking to correct its failures.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The platform pursues equal pay, paid leave and childcare within the existing economy rather than transforming it.

socialized-care.rationale: Liberals back public childcare and pre-kindergarten but not replacing family housework and care with public services; inferred.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Inferred from its civil-liberties stance and support for minority-language access; language purism is not a liberal aim.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred from support for tribal sovereignty and rule-of-law commitments; not examined in the cited sources.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Inferred: liberalism works through existing nation-states, markets and mixed property, not communal property regimes.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred from its commitment to equal rights and non-discrimination, which rules out steering settlement by ethnic group.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Liberals present the mixed economy as a reformed capitalism and reject communism; inferred that they do not see capitalism as failed.

notes: Many answers on foreign policy, drugs, policing and trade reflect a coalition with internal splits; where sources are silent, answers are low-confidence inferences.
